title: Elders and Traditional Leadership
subtitle: Wisdom, responsibility, and guiding the community
body: Among the Murle people, elders have traditionally played an important role in guiding community life. Their knowledge of history, customs, relationships, and past experiences helps younger generations understand their responsibilities.

Leadership is often connected with wisdom, respect, and the ability to bring people together during important moments. Elders help preserve traditions, settle community discussions, and pass cultural knowledge from one generation to another.

Gatherings where elders share stories and advice are important spaces for learning. Through spoken history, young people learn about their identity, family connections, values, and the responsibilities expected of them.
Today, Murle communities continue to balance traditional leadership with modern education and new forms of community organization while protecting the cultural knowledge that connects generations.
